tagline: Link GitHub PRs to ClickUp tasks and auto-update status on merge
metaTitle: GitHub + ClickUp Integration: ClickUp Tasks That Follow PRs
metaDescription: Move ClickUp tasks when PRs open, complete them on merge, and turn GitHub review comments into subtasks. GAIA keeps code and tasks in sync. See the setup steps.
keywords: link GitHub PRs to ClickUp tasks
intro:
Engineering teams use GitHub for code and ClickUp for project management, but keeping the two in sync is a constant manual chore. A developer merges a PR but forgets to update the task status. A project manager moves a task to "In Review" without knowing the PR was already approved. The gap between where the code lives and where the project plan lives creates confusion, duplicated status meetings, and a project board that never reflects reality.

GAIA connects the two so code activity automatically drives task status updates. When a developer opens a pull request linked to a task, GAIA moves the task to "In Review." When the PR merges, GAIA transitions the task to "Done" and notifies the assignee. When a PR is closed without merging, GAIA can revert the task status and leave a comment explaining why. The project board stays accurate without anyone having to remember to update it.

This integration is ideal for software teams that plan work in ClickUp and execute in GitHub. Product managers get a real-time view of engineering progress directly on the project board, while developers focus on writing code rather than updating tickets.

useCases.title: Auto-move ClickUp tasks when PRs are opened
useCases.description: When a developer opens a pull request and references a task ID in the PR title or description, GAIA automatically moves that task to the "In Review" status so project managers see live development progress on the project board.

useCases.title: Complete tasks on PR merge
useCases.description: When a pull request merges to the main branch, GAIA marks the linked task as complete, sets the resolved date, and posts a comment with the merge commit reference so there is a clear audit trail from task to code.

useCases.title: Create subtasks from GitHub review comments
useCases.description: When a code reviewer leaves a change request on a PR, GAIA can create subtasks for each requested change so the work is tracked in the project board and the developer has a structured checklist to address before re-requesting review.

useCases.title: Sync GitHub milestones with ClickUp sprints
useCases.description: GAIA maps milestones to sprints, keeping due dates consistent and automatically moving incomplete tasks to the next sprint when a milestone closes with open issues remaining.

useCases.title: Notify task followers on PR failures
useCases.description: When a GitHub Actions CI run fails on a PR, GAIA posts a comment on the linked task alerting the team that the build is broken, along with a link to the failed run so blockers are visible in the project board immediately.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and ClickUp to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your organization and workspace through GAIA's integrations panel. Select which repositories and spaces or lists should be linked for automated syncing.
Configure how PR states map to task statuses. Tell GAIA which list to use, how to identify the task ID from PR descriptions or branch names, and which status transitions each event should trigger.

howItWorks.step: GAIA syncs code and project status automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA listens to GitHub webhook events and updates tasks in real time. Your board becomes a live reflection of development progress without any manual status updates from the engineering team.

faqs.question: How does GAIA identify which ClickUp task to update from a GitHub PR?
faqs.answer: GAIA can match tasks using a task ID included in the PR title, description, or branch name (e.g., CU-abc123). You can also configure it to match by branch naming conventions or labels. If no match is found, GAIA can create a new task from the PR instead.

faqs.question: Can GAIA handle multiple lists across different repositories?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can map each repository to a specific list or space, so PRs from the frontend repo update the frontend list while backend PRs update a separate list. GAIA manages all mappings from a single configuration.

faqs.question: Does this integration work with custom statuses?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA reads your workspace's custom status definitions and lets you map events to any status in your workflow — whether that's "Code Review," "QA Testing," "Deployed," or any other custom status your team has defined.
